rule: When attaching an OTel context token inside the task-SDK supervisor request handler, place otel_context.attach() inside the try block so the finally clause always detaches it
trigger: otel_context.attach(...) appears before a try block whose finally calls otel_context.detach(token) in supervisor.py or task_runner.py
rationale: If any exception fires between attach() and the try, the token leaks un-detached, corrupting the OTel context chain for subsequent requests on the same thread

evidence.excerpt: token would leak un-detached; move attach inside the try

rule: Document force_flush(timeout_millis=…) call sites with a comment clarifying the value is an upper bound, not a fixed wait
trigger: provider.force_flush(timeout_millis=...) added in task-SDK teardown without an explanatory comment
rationale: Without the comment a future reader benchmarking task teardown may assume every supervisor exit costs the full timeout; force_flush returns as soon as the BSP drains

evidence.excerpt: 5000ms is an upper bound, not a fixed wait — force_flush returns when BSP drains

rule: When wrapping a callable with an OTel detail_span, re-snapshot contextvars after entering the span so operator child spans nest under it rather than being siblings
trigger: contextvars.copy_context() called before a @detail_span or start_as_current_span wrapper in task_runner.py, with ctx.run() used inside the span
rationale: The pre-span snapshot still holds the outer span as current; operator child spans parent to that outer span and appear as siblings of the wrapper span, defeating the telemetry hierarchy

evidence.excerpt: ctx snapshotted before task.execute span; operator spans parent to _execute_task as siblings

rule: When clear_on_success clears task state via a worker backend, also clear asset state accessors for the same task instance
trigger: context["task_state"].clear() called under clear_on_success without a corresponding walk of context["asset_state"] accessors
rationale: Custom worker-side backends may persist asset state externally (e.g. S3); omitting asset_state.clear() leaves orphaned objects even though DB rows are cleared

evidence.excerpt: clear_on_success clears task state but not asset state stored externally by custom backends

rule: Yield one outlet-event record per partition_key rather than a single record with a partition_keys list
trigger: yield {"dest_asset_key": ..., "partition_keys": list(...)} in task_runner.py outlet-event iteration
rationale: The repo is moving away from a plural partition_keys field to avoid ambiguity; each partition should produce its own event record

evidence.excerpt: move away from partition_keys; yield one record per partition_key instead

rule: Docstrings on task-SDK RPC helper methods must exactly match the method's own parameters and return type, not be copied from a sibling method
trigger: A new @staticmethod in task_runner.py whose docstring refers to parameters or return values not present in its own signature
rationale: Copy-pasted docstrings (e.g. get_dag_state reusing get_dagrun_state wording) mislead callers about what the method actually accepts and returns

evidence.excerpt: docstring says 'Return state of the Dag run with the given Run ID' but method only takes dag_id

rule: pytest.param ids must accurately describe the specific scenario under test, including whether parameters have defaults or not
trigger: pytest.param(..., id="...") where the id string claims a parameter property (e.g. 'without_default') that contradicts the actual lambda/function signature
rationale: Misleading ids obscure which edge-case is being exercised and hide gaps where the intended scenario is never actually tested

evidence.excerpt: ID says 'without_default' but all params after b=5 are also defaulted; edge case not exercised

rule: Tests for task-SDK decorator/operator behaviour must assert observable runtime behaviour, not just implementation internals
trigger: A test in test_decorator.py or test_task_runner.py that only asserts on inspect.signature of the original callable or on internal state that was not modified by the fix
rationale: Asserting on unmodified internals gives false confidence; the real invariant is whether the operator behaves correctly at call time (e.g. bind() succeeds or the fix-injected defaults take effect)

evidence.excerpt: inspect.signature returns original callable's signature; fix modifies a local list, not the callable

rule: Include a regression test case using the exact context key names from the original bug report when fixing KNOWN_CONTEXT_KEYS-related decorator issues
trigger: test_construction_succeeds parametrize cases added for a KNOWN_CONTEXT_KEYS bug fix without a case using actual context key names like start_date or end_date
rationale: Without the exact scenario the regression test does not guard against re-introduction of the specific bug (#56128: foo(start_date, end_date) called with (None, None))

evidence.excerpt: add a case using actual context key names as regression for issue #56128

rule: Use mock.create_autospec() when monkeypatching DAG or operator methods in task-SDK tests
trigger: monkeypatch.setattr(DAG, "...", mock.MagicMock()) without spec= or autospec= in task-sdk tests
rationale: Airflow's testing guidelines require autospecced mocks for DAG/operator methods to catch signature mismatches at test time

evidence.excerpt: use create_autospec; aligns with Airflow's testing guidelines and catches signature mistakes

rule: Prefer the conf_vars context manager over unittest.mock.patch for overriding Airflow configuration values in tests
trigger: with patch("airflow.sdk.configuration.conf.get", ...) or patch("airflow.configuration.conf.get", ...) in task-sdk tests
rationale: conf_vars is the idiomatic Airflow mechanism for test-scoped config overrides; patch bypasses the config system and can break when the import path changes

evidence.excerpt: why mocking this rather than using conf_vars context manager?

rule: Remove unused test helper functions rather than leaving them as dead code in test modules
trigger: A helper function defined in a test class or module in task-sdk/tests/ that is not called by any test in the same file
rationale: Dead helpers increase cognitive load and make test intent harder to scan; reviewers must verify the helper is truly unused before trusting the test coverage

evidence.excerpt: _make_provider_with_detail_level added but not used; increases noise and obscures test intent

rule: Mark tests that rely on POSIX dup2 semantics with pytest.mark.skipif(os.name == 'nt', ...) to prevent Windows CI failures
trigger: os.dup2(socket.fileno(), 0/1/2) used inside a test class in test_supervisor.py without a platform guard
rationale: Windows sockets are not CRT file descriptors; dup2 onto stdio with a socket fails on Windows and would break cross-platform CI

evidence.excerpt: add skipif(os.name=='nt'); dup2 socket onto stdio fails on Windows

rule: In task-SDK signal-forwarding integration tests, use a short time.sleep (≤2s) so the test exits promptly on SIGTERM rather than waiting out the full supervisor watchdog window
trigger: time.sleep(N) with N > 5 inside an execute() method of a test operator in a signal_forward_test.py or similar integration test DAG
rationale: PEP 475 resumes sleep after a signal handler returns; a long sleep means the test blocks for the full watchdog period and only exits on SIGKILL

evidence.excerpt: time.sleep(30) ties up the full watchdog window; drop to 2s so test exits on SIGTERM promptly

rule: OTel span tests in task-sdk must assert parent/child span relationships, not just that a named span exists
trigger: Test in test_task_runner.py asserts 'task.execute' in [s.name for s in exporter.get_finished_spans()] without checking span.parent.span_id
rationale: A suite that only checks span existence stays green even if the wrapping span ends up a sibling of operator child spans rather than their parent, hiding the telemetry nesting regression

evidence.excerpt: suite stays green even if task.execute is a sibling; assert span.parent.span_id to catch nesting bugs

rule: The TS-SDK log channel must buffer log records emitted before the coordinator socket is connected and flush them once connected, not drop or only write to stderr
trigger: LogChannel.write() or equivalent in ts-sdk returns early or writes only to stderr when connected===false, with no buffering logic
rationale: Logs emitted during TS subprocess startup (before the comms socket handshake completes) are otherwise permanently lost; Go and Java SDKs both implement this pre-connection buffer

evidence.excerpt: buffer logs at stage 2 before connected; Go and Java SDKs both handle this lifecycle

rule: TS-SDK TaskInstance public context must locate a task instance by the dag/run/task/map tuple, aligned with Go and Java SDK identity, rather than exposing a raw taskInstanceId
trigger: readonly taskInstanceId: string added to the public TaskInstance interface in ts-sdk/src/task.ts
rationale: Neither the Go SDK (DagID/RunID/TaskID/MapIndex) nor the Java SDK exposes a raw TI id on the context; diverging breaks cross-SDK consistency for coordinator XCom addressing

evidence.excerpt: Go and Java SDKs locate TI by dag/run/task/map tuple; taskInstanceId diverges from cross-SDK alignment
